svg.title: What GPUs do for AI in four panels. CPU versus GPU: four large cores and a cache against a grid of small cores organised in SMs, blocks and warps of 32; Python loops versus NumPy hundreds to thousands of times faster. Tensor cores: H100 dense TFLOPS on a log scale, FP64 34, TF32 495, BF16 990, FP8 1,980, so FP8 is about 60 times FP64; Rubin reaches 35 PFLOPS NVFP4. The memory wall: 990 TFLOPS over 3.35 TB/s means about 295 operations per byte to stay busy, but writing a token is about 1 per byte, so one H100 tops out near 209 tokens per second for an 8B 16-bit model, 838 at 4-bit, 24 for 70B. Scale out: a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack of 72 GPUs with 20.7 TB of HBM4. Below: the main optimisation is moving less data.
svg.text: Thousands of simple cores, limited by how fast memory feeds them
≈ 295 ops per byte to keep busy
THE MAIN OPTIMISATION IS MOVING LESS DATA
